experiment: Phase V2 transition sweep: where does induction appear/disappear in width, per architecture? Cells (3 seeds each): slots at depth 2 widths 32/64/256, predicate at width 32, vanilla at width 192. Train with the V1 slice's default invocations; induction scored by the same ladder battery (probe-seed mean vs planted-oracle floor) as V1.
registered: 2026-08-10 17:40 UTC, before any cell was trained

predictions.claim: Slots at width 64 still inducts: 3/3 seeds above their own floors.
Slots at width 32 does not: at most 1/3 seeds above floor (the transition for the partition sits between 32 and 64).
Predicate at width 32 still inducts (majority of seeds above floor) — its mechanism is handed over by named scalars, not bought with width.
Slots at width 256 stays above floor (the advantage coexists with the plain model's own induction rather than being displaced by it).
Vanilla at width 192 inducts at 2/3 or more seeds (the plain transition sits below 192, not between 192 and 256).

decision_rule: X1+X2 date the partition's transition an octave below the plain model's; X3 separates handed-over structure from capacity; X4 failing would resurrect the displacement story V1 retracted; X5 locates the plain transition for the width-vs-depth story. Ladders run on every cell regardless of verdicts — interpretation is the deliverable.
